cards.title: What stays exactly as it is
items: One generic 401 for both unknown identifier and wrong password — auth.service.ts:128-130
Strict DTO validation, so a client-supplied role is rejected — auth.controller.ts:40-50
Store suspension refused at login and again on every request — auth.service.ts:148-159
Demoting or deactivating the last owner is refused — auth.service.ts:296-343

cards.title: Gaps this flow closes
items: JWT_SECRET is unset, so tokens are signed with a constant in the repo — app.module.ts:144-157
No per-account lockout: 120 attempts per minute per IP — main.ts:131-154
REDIS_URL is blank, so counters would fall back to process memory — redis.ts:72-76
No revocation, so a stolen token stays valid for its full 7 days — auth.domain.ts:31-33
phoneVerified is never enforced, and 8 characters is the whole password policy — auth.service.ts:75
Failed logins are never recorded; SecurityIncident requires a storeId, so AuditLog is the right sink

cards.title: Nothing becomes a session early
items: Forced password change yields a 5-minute ticket, not a token
MFA for owner and platform roles runs before any cookie is set
The password policy moves past a bare 8-character minimum

cards.title: Why it is worth the rework
items: The refresh cookie is httpOnly, so injected script cannot read it
Rotation makes a stolen refresh token detectable the moment it is reused
A deactivated member or changed role loses access at once, because the database decides
Every attempt is auditable through AuditLog, including platform logins
